enonce_markdown: A programmer writes, at the top of a function in a source file, a short comment that says what the function does and what each parameter means. This is an example of:
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Documentation written inside the source code for the next programmer is internal technical documentation; documents written for end users are user documentation.

### Solution

A comment inside the code that explains the purpose and parameters of a function helps the programmers who will read and maintain the code. It is **technical documentation held inside the source code**. A user manual and an installation guide are separate documents, and a test plan describes how the software will be tested.

choix.texte: Technical documentation held inside the source code

enonce_markdown: A cashier in a supermarket in Yaounde has to learn how to print the daily sales report with a new application. Which document should she consult?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

User documentation explains how to operate the software for its everyday users, with step-by-step instructions.

### Solution

The cashier needs step-by-step instructions on how to use the application, which is found in the **user guide**. A data dictionary and a system flowchart are technical documents for developers, and a source code listing is only meaningful to programmers.

enonce_markdown: Which of the following would be found in the technical documentation of a system rather than in the user documentation?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Technical documentation serves those who build and maintain the system (design diagrams, data structures, code). User documentation serves those who use it (instructions, screenshots, troubleshooting).

### Solution

An entity-relationship diagram and the data dictionary describe how the data are structured; they are used by developers and maintainers, so they are **technical documentation**. The step-by-step tutorial with screenshots, the troubleshooting guide and the list of error messages with the action to take are all intended for the user.

choix.texte: A step-by-step tutorial with screenshots of each screen
A troubleshooting guide for common problems
An entity-relationship diagram and data dictionary of the database
A list of error messages with the action the user should take

enonce_markdown: A new programmer is hired to correct a fault in an application that was developed three years ago by a team that has left the company. Which documentation will help her most in finding where to make the correction?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

A maintainer needs to know how the system is built: its structure, data and code. That information is in the technical documentation, not in the user documentation.

### Solution

The technical documentation (design diagrams, data dictionary, commented source code, test results) shows how the system is built and where each function is located, so it is the most useful here. The user manual and a quick reference card explain how to operate the program, and a licence agreement only gives the legal terms of use.

choix.texte: The technical documentation, including design diagrams, data dictionary and commented code
A quick reference card for the keyboard shortcuts

enonce_markdown:
A school in Limbe is about to start using a new fees management program.

(a) Give three items that the user documentation should contain. (3 marks)

(b) Give three items that the technical documentation should contain. (3 marks)

(c) State two reasons why documentation must be updated when the program is modified. (2 marks)
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Ask who reads the document and what that person must do. The user must operate the system; the maintainer must understand and modify it.

### Solution

**(a) User documentation (any three):** how to start the program and log in; how to record a payment and print a receipt; how to produce a list of students who owe fees (with screenshots); the meaning of each error message; a troubleshooting guide or frequently asked questions; a contact for help.

**(b) Technical documentation (any three):** the system flowcharts or data flow diagrams; the data dictionary and the structure of the tables or files; the commented source code; the hardware and software requirements and installation steps; the test plans and test results.

**(c)** (i) Out-of-date documents no longer describe the real system, so users make mistakes or maintainers misunderstand the code and introduce faults. (ii) It saves time and cost for later changes, and keeps the system usable if the people who know it leave.

### Method reminder

Good internal documentation states the purpose (why and what), the meaning of the parameters and the assumptions or limits, rather than repeating the instructions one by one.

### Solution

Testing the function (a run gives `12.0` for the list 10, 12, 14 and raises `ZeroDivisionError` for an empty list) shows that it returns the mean of the values and fails when the list is empty. The best comment is the one that gives the purpose, the parameter and the precondition: **"# Returns the mean of the marks in list m. m must not be empty, otherwise ZeroDivisionError is raised."** The first option only repeats what the code already says, the second only gives a name, and the last is too vague to be of any use.

choix.texte: # Adds the items of m and then divides the total by the number of items in m.
